quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: When you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, you must yield. Wait until it is safe, then you may go.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance is affected.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, affects your judgment of speed and distance, reduces recovery from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn you about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on. Other drivers must be able to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on roads with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights are at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers know what you plan to do in advance.

questions.question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal to the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down. This helps the passing vehicle move back into the right lane safely.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: An "End school zone" sign marks the end of a reduced speed zone. Follow the school zone speed limit only during the times shown on the sign.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility of vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beam headlights. Use low beams instead—they light up the road and objects better in foggy conditions.

questions.question: When parallel parking, park your car within ____ of the curb.
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches
questions.explanation: Your car should be no more than 12 inches from the curb when parallel parking. Always park where drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: You are turning left at a busy intersection. Oncoming traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up as soon as the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as regular driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A series of curves is ahead.
The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes very slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake pedal with steady pressure. Pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: Using which of the following greatly increases your crash risk?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone (even hands-free), radio, or CD player can distract you from driving and increase your crash risk.

questions.question: What should a driver do if they see an animal on the road?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What should you do when another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you are tailgated and a right lane is open, move to it. If no right lane is available, wait until the road ahead is clear and then slowly reduce your speed. This will encourage the tailgater to pass you. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What should a small vehicle driver be prepared for when passing a large vehicle?

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles out of their lane. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer correctly when passing or approaching large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What must you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave to let the emergency vehicle pass.
Merge to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move immediately to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, what is the safest way to pass a cyclist?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with enough space between you and the cyclist.
Continue straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign before passing.
Honk to tell the cyclist you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with enough space between you and the cyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist the same way you pass any vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups of cyclists. Do not honk, as it may startle the cyclist and cause a crash.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks without signals or gates in a line of traffic, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can completely cross the tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can completely cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: When following another vehicle at railroad tracks, make sure you have room to cross completely before entering the tracks. Never pass another vehicle at or near a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: What must you do when you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you do not drive next to it.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass it quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes so you do not drive next to it.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes if safe to do so. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give it as much space as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a steady green traffic light?

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a steady green light, let pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection pass first. You may continue driving, but slow down if the light might change before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Move to a different lane or slow down.
Pull off the road behind the vehicle.
Move to the lane closest to the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane or slow down.
questions.explanation: The Move Over Law protects police, firefighters, tow truck drivers, sanitation workers, and utility workers on the roadside. You must move away from the lane closest to the stopped emergency vehicle. If you cannot move over safely, you must slow down.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another vehicle is coming toward you or in front of you at night. Switch to low beams to keep everyone safe on the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: When driving near a blind person using a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane is ending ahead.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive faster because they are more alert.
Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness make it harder to drive safely. These feelings distract your mind from the road. Take time to calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: You can avoid alcohol-related crashes by:

options.text: Deciding not to drive before you drink.
Saying no to a drink if you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after drinking starts.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of the above.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Food in your stomach slows down alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest way is to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Always drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit.
